newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-WARNE, MCGRATH BLAST AWAY WEST INDIES TOP ORDER.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-WARNE, MCGRATH BLAST AWAY WEST INDIES TOP ORDER.

text.p: Legspinner Shane Warne and fast bowler Glenn McGrath blasted away four of the West Indies' top order batsman to put Australia in a dominant position at lunch on the first day of their fourth test match on Saturday.
Warne took the prize wicket of an in-form Brian Lara (9) with his first ball to the left-hander, delighting a capacity crowd of over 20,000 at the tree-lined and sun-drenched Adelaide Oval.
The West Indies were at 82 for five after 28 overs at lunch.
Warne took two wickets for seven runs in his first two overs, including that of Chivnarine Chanderpaul (20) who has been the West Indies' most consistent batsman on tour.
Lara, who scored 295 runs in his first three limited overs innings of the New Year, appeared to bat like he was still playing one-day cricket, trying to slog Warne over mid-off for six.
He succeeded only in gently lofting the ball into Greg Blewett's hands at mid-off.
Glenn McGrath was at his fiery best from the start of the West Indies innings after captain Courtney Walsh won the toss and elected to bat on what had seemed a good batting wicket.
But McGrath extracted extra bounce and some slight sideways movement to tempt opener Sherwin Campbell (0) into nicking one to wicketkeeper Ian Healy in the fith over.
Fellow opener and test debutante Adrian Griffith soon followed, caught plumb leg before wicket to fellow debutante Andrew Bichel in the eighth over with the score at 22.
McGrath struck again with a brute of ball that threatened to rip out Carl Hooper's throat before he got the edge of his bat to the ball which flew to Mark Waugh at second slip.
The West Indies are also expected to struggle when they bowl, which will probably be in the final session or early on the second day given their long batting tail.
Strike fast bowler Curtly Ambrose, the chief destroyer for the West Indies in their third test win in Melbourne, was forced to withdraw after failing a morning fitness test with a strained groin.
The West Indies have also lost paceman Kenny Benjamin, who returned earlier this month with a side strain.
Ambrose and Benjamin have been replaced by Cameron Cuffy and Patterson Thompson, who have three test matches of experience between them.
Australia lead the five test series 2-1 and only need to draw or win this match to retain the Frank Worrell Trophy.
